slot.brief: Determine whether a given piecewise-defined or rational function is one-one/onto, or check reflexivity/symmetry/transitivity of a relation on a small set.

verdicts.working: If f(a)=f(b), cross-multiplication gives 3a=3b, so f is one-one. The value 2 is never attained, so f is not onto ℝ.

working:
For y in R, y = (2x + 1)/(x - 1) gives y(x - 1) = 2x + 1, so x(y - 2) = y + 1. Thus x = (y + 1)/(y - 2), which exists for every y except y = 2. Hence the range is R - {2}, so f is not onto. Also f'(x) = -3/(x - 1)^2 < 0 for all x in the domain, so f is strictly decreasing and therefore one-one.

Independent check: If f(a)=f(b), cross-multiplication gives 3a=3b, so f is one-one. The value 2 is never attained, so f is not onto ℝ.
solution: If $f(a)=f(b)$, then cross-multiplication gives $3a=3b$, so $a=b$ and $f$ is one-one. For $y=f(x)$, $x=\dfrac{y+1}{y-2}$, which is undefined at $y=2$; hence the range is $\mathbb{R}\setminus\{2\}$ and $f$ is not onto.
